title: Crash density: painted vs. protected lanes
description: Painted-only bike lanes see 16.7 cyclist crashes per km vs 17.2 on protected lanes — 1.0x the density, raw counts not normalized by ridership.
caveat: Raw counts overrepresent high-traffic corridors; no volume normalization. Dooring crashes are undercounted citywide.

title: Highest crash-density corridors
description: Top corridors by cyclist crashes per km of bikeway: Kinzie (77.46/km); Wells (50.82/km); Clark (45.66/km); Milwaukee (42.73/km); Dearborn (37.44/km).
caveat: Raw counts, not normalized by bike volume. Dooring is undercounted.

title: Ward concentration
description: 5 of 50 wards account for 27% of located cyclist crashes: Ward 27 (1186), Ward 42 (1092), Ward 32 (820), Ward 1 (817), Ward 34 (656).
caveat: Ward totals reflect where people ride most, not only where streets are worst.

title: Dooring: the number that is too low
description: Only 2031 crashes carry a dooring flag. Dooring is structurally excluded from 'reportable' crash records unless damage/injury thresholds are met, so true dooring risk — especially on painted-lane corridors — is higher than any number on this site.
caveat: Structural undercount; treat as a floor, never a rate.

title: What cyclists collide with
description: Most common motor-vehicle unit types in cyclist crashes: Passenger (11396), Sport Utility Vehicle (Suv) (2730), Unknown/Na (1542).
caveat: Unit types as recorded by responding officers; fleet mix not normalized.
